en.name: Muffins, commercially packaged
en.summary: Commercially packaged muffins keep 3–7 days at room temperature in their sealed pack, and 3 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Refrigeration is not recommended — a muffin dries out and goes stale quickly in the fridge.
en.pantry: 3–7 days in the unopened pack at room temperature, somewhere cool and out of direct sun, and to the printed date if that comes sooner. A packaged muffin lasts noticeably longer than a bakery one because it is made with more fat and sugar, sealed in a low-oxygen pack and often carries a mould inhibitor. Once you open the pack, close it properly or move the muffins to a tub — an open pack goes stale at the cut surface first, and a muffin with a fresh-fruit or cream-cheese topping is a perishable food that belongs in the fridge regardless of what the base timeline says.
en.fridge: Refrigeration is not recommended: a muffin will quickly dry out and become stale in the fridge. The reason is starch retrogradation, which runs fastest just above freezing — the crumb firms and dries faster at 4 °C than it does on the counter. The one thing the fridge buys is time against mould, which matters in a hot humid kitchen, and if that is your problem the freezer solves it better by stopping mould without the staling penalty. Warming a stale muffin briefly does reverse some of the staling; it does nothing about mould.
en.freezer: 3 months at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. Freeze them in their pack or wrapped individually with the air excluded, so you can take out one at a time. Kept continuously frozen they stay safe well beyond that window — the timeline describes dryness, ice crystals and freezer burn, not safety. Thaw at room temperature in the wrapping, or warm a frozen muffin in a low oven for a few minutes.
en.thawing: Thaw wrapped at room temperature for an hour or two, or warm from frozen in a low oven. A muffin thawed in the fridge and still cold may be refrozen with some quality loss; one thawed on a warm counter should not be refrozen.
spoilage: Fuzzy mould spots, often first in the crease where the paper case meets the crumb.
A stale, dry crumb that crumbles to dust instead of tearing.
A rancid or crayon-like smell from the fat in an old muffin.
A sticky or wet surface inside a pack that has been opened and resealed damp.
tips: Go by the printed date first; that is what the pack is for.
Wrap individually before freezing so you take out only what you need.
Muffins with fresh fruit, cream cheese or custard toppings belong in the fridge.
Peel the paper case off before freezing if you plan to warm them in an oven.

faq.q: How long do packaged muffins last?
faq.a: 3–7 days at room temperature in the sealed pack, or to the printed date if it is sooner. Frozen, 3 months at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Should muffins go in the fridge?
faq.a: No. Refrigeration is not recommended because they dry out and go stale quickly. Freeze them instead if you need more time.
Yes, 3 months at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. Wrap them individually and thaw at room temperature or warm from frozen.

zh.name: 市售包裝瑪芬
zh.summary: 市售包裝瑪芬未拆封放室溫可放 3～7 天，−18 °C 冷凍是 3 個月。不建議冷藏——瑪芬在冷藏室裡會很快變乾走味。
zh.pantry: 未拆封、放陰涼避免直曬的地方，室溫 3～7 天；若包裝上的印製日期更早，就以日期為準。包裝瑪芬明顯比麵包店現做的耐放，因為它油糖比例更高、封在低氧包裝裡，而且常常含有抑霉成分。一旦拆封就要確實封好，或把瑪芬移到保鮮盒——拆開的包裝會先從切面開始變乾；另外，表面有新鮮水果或奶油乳酪裝飾的那種是易腐食品，不管基本期限寫什麼，都該放冷藏。
zh.fridge: 不建議冷藏：瑪芬放冷藏會很快變乾、走味。原因是澱粉回凝，而回凝在略高於冰點時跑得最快——在 4 °C 下，組織會比放在檯面上更快變硬變乾。冷藏唯一買得到的是對抗霉的時間，這在又熱又濕的廚房裡有意義；但如果你的問題是霉，冷凍解決得更好，因為它擋得住霉又不必付老化的代價。稍微加熱可以逆轉一部分老化，但對霉一點用也沒有。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 3 個月品質最好。連包裝一起冷凍，或一顆一顆包好、擠掉空氣，之後要幾顆拿幾顆。只要全程沒退冰，超過這個期限仍然安全——期限描述的是變乾、冰晶和凍燒，不是安全。要吃時包著在室溫解凍，或直接從冷凍進低溫烤箱烤幾分鐘。
zh.thawing: 包著在室溫放一兩個小時解凍，或直接從冷凍用低溫烤箱回溫。在冷藏解凍、而且還是冰的可以再冷凍，只是品質會打折；在溫暖檯面上解凍過的就不要再凍回去。
spoilage: 長出絨毛狀霉點，常常先出現在紙模和蛋糕體交界的摺縫裡。
組織乾到一捏成粉，撕不出組織感。
聞得到油耗味、像蠟筆的氣味。
拆封後受潮又封回去，表面變得黏手或濕濕的。
tips: 先看包裝上的印製日期，那就是包裝存在的意義。
冷凍前一顆一顆包好，要幾顆拿幾顆。
有新鮮水果、奶油乳酪或卡士達裝飾的瑪芬要放冷藏。
打算用烤箱回溫的話，冷凍前先把紙模撕掉。

faq.a: 未拆封放室溫 3～7 天，或以更早的印製日期為準。冷凍則是 −18 °C 下 3 個月。
不要。冷藏會讓它很快變乾走味，所以不建議。需要更長時間就冷凍。
可以，−18 °C 下 3 個月品質最好。一顆一顆包好冷凍，室溫解凍或直接從冷凍回溫都行。
